To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

IGF-I and IGFBP mRNA levels in the liver of adult undernourised rats were recovered by insulin and refeeding administration, with no prior restoration to control values of serum and pitutary GH and no compensatory change in GH receptor gene exresssion."

1) IGF-I and IGF-binding proteins mRNA expression are decreased in adult undernoushied rats; 2) IGF-I, IGFBP-1, and IGFBP-2 mRNA expression are restored by insulin treatment; 3) IGF-I expression is also restored by refeeding, while IGFBP-3 expression is not; and 4) GH receptor mRNA expression is not affected by insulin or refeeding

insulin and nutrients are able to restore liver mRNA expression of both IGF-I and its binding proteins in adult undernoured diabetic rats without prior restoration of pituitary and serum GH and with no compensatory changes of liver GH receptor gene expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the regulation of the IGF axis and its relationship to GH in the rat.
the role played by GH and nutrients on the regulation of the IGF system in adult rats.
the regulation of GH/IGF-I axis in undernourished rats and the role of nutrients and insulin in the regulation of this axis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the regulation of IGF-I secretion is complex and that it involves the interaction of several factors, including nutrients, insulin, and GH.
GH is a major regulator of IGF-I gene expression in liver and that the effects of insulin, nutrients and GH are synergistic.
IGF-I and its binding proteins are regulated by GH and insulin in adult undernoushied diabetic rats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the adult, GH is not the major regulator of the IGF-I axis, but that it is a necessary component of the complex regulatory mechanism.
GH is a major determinant of the regulation of IGF-I gene expression in the liver and that other factors, such as nutrients or insulin, can also play a role.
the GH/IGF-I axis is a key factor for the recovery of IGF-I secretion in undernourished animals, but it is not the only one.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IGF-I system can be restored in the absence of GH.
insulin and nutrients are the key regulators of IGF-I expression in the adult liver.
insulin and nutrients administration can restore serum and liver IGF-I levels in adult undernousished diabetic rats without a previous increase of pituitary GH secretion.
